flags.text: stopScanning (called on pairing-screen disappear) does not reset pendingScanRequest. If the user opened the screen while Bluetooth was not poweredOn (startScanning/rescan set pendingScanRequest=true) and left, the next poweredOn runs radioCameUp → startScanning → an open AllowDuplicates scan with no screen to stop it, contradicting the design note that discovery scans run only while the pairing screen is open.

docs/USERS_MANUAL.md says the app 'stops scanning aggressively when the Watch app backgrounds', but the connector has no scenePhase/background hook: discovery stops only when the pairing view disappears (stopScanning) and a deferred pendingScanRequest can still start a scan later with no screen open.

flags.text: Second 2A37 parser beside HeartRateMeasurement.parse (iOS). The iOS one rounds each RR to whole ms to match the Polar SDK, and its doc says a 1 ms difference moves every HRV figure; this one sends unrounded Double ms (raw*1000/1024). The Watch RRs go via watchStrapSample into pendingWatchStrapRR and are drained into the workout recorder, so a workout fed by the Watch strap path uses RR values that differ from the phone path by up to 0.5 ms. Lost-contact and HR==0 handling also differ (iOS keeps them).

No test references parseHeartRateMeasurement or WatchStrapConnector (grep of EmuquTests/EmuquUITests); the lost-contact, HR 0, energy-expended and RR paths are untested, unlike the iOS HeartRateMeasurement parser (EmuquTests/HeartRateMeasurementTests.swift).
